Cisco will now suit up for his third NFL team after spending time with the Jaguars and Jets since entering the league in 2021. In 80 regular-season games, the 26-year-old has accumulated 293 total tackles (197 solo), including 2.5 sacks, and four forced fumbles. Although Detroit expects Kerby Joseph (knee) to be back on the field soon, Cisco will provide much-needed depth at the safety position.

Bates was able to make multiple field goals for the third straight game after having done so just once over the team's first five contests this year. The kicker converted attempts from 28 and 40 yards in the first half before adding makes from 33 and 43 yards after the break. Bates has now gone 16-for-17 on field-goal tries while making all 24 of his PATs over eight games during the 2026 campaign to this point.

Williams and the rest of the Lions' air attack had a quiet afternoon, as Jared Goff threw for just 170 yards overall. Williams was efficient on his two touches, but he finished with a new season low in receiving yards. The 2022 first-round pick, who's averaging 16.7 yards per reception on the season, will likely be busier in a Week 10 matchup against the Patriots in Germany next Sunday.

Goff was the latest quarterback to scuffle some against a Dolphins defense that's fought hard all season, as the veteran signal-caller took three sacks and finished with a new season low in passing yards. Goff also failed to throw a touchdown for the first time this season, and he threw a pick for the second time in as many games after going without an interception for the first six contests of the campaign. Goff has completed at least 68.0 percent of his passes in three straight games heading into a Week 10 matchup against the Patriots in Germany next Sunday.

St. Brown set the pace across the board for the Lions in receptions, receiving yards and targets. St. Brown was playing through a rib issue that had limited him throughout the practice week, but he turned in an efficient effort that included his fifth straight game with six or more catches. St. Brown's touchdown drought did extend to five games, and he'll once again aim to snap it in next Sunday's Week 10 matchup against the Patriots in Germany.

It was a relatively quiet day by Gibbs' lofty standards against a Dolphins team that's proven to have plenty of fight despite its losing record. The standout back salvaged his fantasy day with an eight-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter, Gibbs' second score on the ground in as many games and ninth overall. Gibbs failed to record at least one reception for the first time this season, but he's already amassed 1,132 scrimmage yards and 11 total touchdowns across eight games heading into next Sunday's showdown against the Patriots in Germany.

Campbell suffered a neck injury while making a tackle in the third quarter of last Sunday's win over Minnesota and remains in the hospital. Detroit head coach Dan Campbell shared Friday that the linebacker continues to improve, but  his placement on IR means he'll miss at least the team's next four games. K.J. Britt, who Detroit signed off New England's practice squad Wednesday, may be asked to immediately step into a starting role.

With consecutive full practices to close out Week 9 prep, Branch has officially cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol. The starting strong safety is all set to suit up for Sunday's game alongside free safety Chuck Clark.

injuries.detail: This move was anticipated, as Rolder suffered a season-ending hamstring injury in the Lions' win over Minnesota on Sunday. The rookie linebacker logged a career-high 17 defensive snaps and notched his first NFL sack in that contest, so his injury comes at an unfortunate time. Rolder will now turn his focus toward rehabbing the injury in order to be ready for offseason activities in 2027.

McCreary wasn't listed on the injury report Wednesday or Thursday but practiced in a limited capacity Friday. As a result, the 26-year-old was listed as questionable for the divisional showdown with Minnesota, though he has since been cleared to suit up. McCreary has appeared in all six of Detroit's regular-season games in 2026, amassing 22 total tackles (17 solo), 1.0 sacks and one forced fumble.

Rakestraw suffered an ankle injury late in this past Sunday's win over Green Bay. He was held to limited practice sessions Wednesday and Thursday but was able to upgrade to full participation Friday. As such, Rakestraw is good to go for Sunday's big battle against Minnesota.

Pacheco has been sidelined for the entirety of the regular season to this point after undergoing back surgery in September. Sione Vaki has been working as the Lions' clear RB2, though Jahmyr Gibbs has been a true workhorse out of the backfield. If Pacheco does return at the end of the regular season, it's hard to envision him having a big impact coming off back surgery.

Jordan Love threw for a massive 372 yards in the victory, but Smith wasn't targeted on any of the quarterback's 29 passes. That's been par for the course this season -- Smith has drawn one or zero targets in five straight appearances. The veteran tight end has had some productive offensive seasons in his career, but it appears Smith isn't going to be a big part of the Packers' passing-game plans this year.

With Josh Jacobs (finger) knocked out of the game in the first quarter and set to miss several weeks, Strong figures to see his role expand in Green Bay's backfield, though MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and even Chris Brooks (ankle) are likely to also see snaps in the coming weeks. Strong is not a recommended fantasy target in 12-team leagues.

After being a healthy inactive for the Packers' previous two games, Johnson suited up for Sunday's tilt with the Patriots while Lloyd was inactive. With Jacobs leaving the contest late in the first quarter after fracturing his right ring finger, Johnson was thrust into action and delivered the Packers' best rushing performance of the season, finishing with 14 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown in the 45-27 win. Head coach Matt LaFleur relayed Monday that Jacobs will need surgery and could land on injured reserve, and while Lloyd could have a chance at returning to action Week 10, the Packers likely came away encouraged enough by Johnson's showing in Foxborough to give him another turn as their lead option on the ground. Johnson isn't likely to earn much passing-down work, however, as Lloyd, Pierre Strong and Chris Brooks (ankle) -- who could return from IR this week -- are all more capable options in that phase.

Brooks -- who last played in Week 4 -- was designated to return from injured reserve this past Wednesday and listed as questionable ahead of Week 9. Though the Packers held off on activating Brooks for Sunday's win over the Patriots, he could be needed more than expected going forward, with Josh Jacobs in line to miss time with a finger injury that may result in an IR stint.

Smack put together one of the more impressive performances of his rookie campaign. The kicker converted a 41-yard field goal in the second quarter before later adding makes from 51 and 38 yards in the second half. Smack entered Week 9 having made just five of his last nine field-goal tries, so Sunday's performance was a much-needed one for the 23-year-old.

The athletic tight end didn't get in on any of the fun on a day when Jordan Love threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns. Kraft's stat line set (receptions, receiving yards) or tied (targets) season lows, while his work on the ground included a pair of season-high figures. Nevertheless, it was an utterly forgettable showing for Kraft, who'll look to atone in a Week 10 home divisional clash against the Vikings next Sunday.

Golden led the Packers in receptions and targets while finishing second in receiving yards, and the latter total was also a new career high. The second-year wideout also laid claim to the game's longest catch (49 yards), and he reeled in the first of Jordan Love's three TD passes on the day with a five-yard grab at just under the eight-minute mark of the first quarter. Golden now has four 100-yard efforts in what is already a breakout campaign that's seen him amass a 53-783-5 line on 92 targets heading into a Week 10 home showdown against the Vikings next Sunday.

Watson repeatedly got the best of Christian Gonzalez and the rest of a talented Patriots secondary, recording team- and career-high receiving yardage totals along the way. Watson burned New England for four catches of 20-plus yards, including a game-long 49-yard grab, as well as a 39-yard touchdown reception in the latter portion of the third quarter. Watson's career-best line is up to a tally of 49-879-7 on 74 targets heading into a Week 10 home matchup against the Vikings next Sunday.

Love continued to attack downfield with great efficacy in the significant road upset for the Packers. Love averaged 12.8 yards per attempt while amassing his second-highest passing yardage total of the season, a figure bested only by the 387-yard tally he managed in Week 1. Love generated his second straight three-touchdown day through the air as well, connecting with Matthew Golden (five yards), Savion Williams (10 yards) and Christian Watson (39 yards) for his trio of scoring strikes and kicking off the scoring on the day with a 13-yard rush just 1:41 into the contest. Love is up to 2,618 passing yards with a 19:6 TD:INT and a pair of rushing scores heading into a Week 10 home divisional clash against the Vikings next Sunday.

Williams was able to reel in multiple passes for the third time in four games since returning from injured reserve following an ankle injury. The wide receiver's biggest moment of the game came in the third quarter when he secured a 10-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Jordan Love by making an acrobatic catch. Williams has now reeled in 11 of 13 targets for 109 yards and a touchdown while turning eight carries into 44 yards over four contests this season.

Melton wasn't targeted prior to departing, but he did return four kicks for 110 yards. J. Michael Sturdivant will be next up for wideout snaps behind Matthew Golden, Christian Watson and Savion Williams.
Hopper suffered a significant chest injury in the first quarter of Sunday's game. The inside linebacker has been ruled out, leaving Nick Niemann to finish the game in his stead.

Nixon ended Week 9 prep as a limited participant. The cornerback appears to be set to play through a persistent groin injury in Sunday's contest, meaning he may share his defensive snaps against the Patriots with Benjamin St-Juste.

Banks' consistent limited participation throughout Week 9 prep has enabled the left guard to dodge any injury designation for Sunday's showdown. The left guard is all set to suit up as a vital part of a Packers offensive line that has sustained extensive injuries over the first eight weeks of the 2026 regular season.

After the Packers designated Parsons for return from injured reserve Wednesday, he logged three straight limited sessions as he ramps up for his first game action since Dec. 14, 2025 in Denver, when he tore the ACL in his left knee. Parsons himself told Ryan Wood of USA Today that he won't "pinpoint a day" for his return, but his 21-day window conveniently ends on Wednesday, Nov. 25, when the Packers take on the Rams in Los Angeles.

McDuffie tied with Evan Williams for the team lead in tackles. He played every one of the Packers' defensive snaps for the second straight game in the absence of Zaire Franklin (shin). McDuffie has tallied 21 tackles in the pair of contests, so he's looking like a strong IDP option, at least for as long as Franklin remains sidelined.

Williams finished tied for the team lead in takedowns with linebacker Isaiah McDuffie, notching double-digit stops for the fourth time this season. The safety has now compiled 71 total tackles (44 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding six passes defensed, two of which are interceptions, and a fumble recovery over the first eight games of the 2026 campaign.

Wyatt was listed as questionable heading into this contest due to an ankle injury. However, he is cleared to suit up for Week 8 versus Carolina. The 28-year-old has appeared in seven regular-season games during the 2026 campaign, amassing 18 total tackles (10 solo) and 2.0 sacks.

Since the Texans had built their lead to 19 with less than five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, head coach DeMeco Ryans opted to pull starting quarterback C.J. Stroud from the game and handed the offense over to Mills. In what marked his first playing time of the season, Mills directed two possessions. He led the Texans to a field goal with 2:20 remaining, then knelt the ball twice to run out the clock when Houston got the ball back with 1:07 left. With Stroud enjoying a bounce-back campaign, Mills' opportunities will likely be limited to garbage-time situations so long as Stroud stays healthy.

Week 9 marked the first time all season that Stover sat out, with the Texans opting to keep their other four tight ends (Dalton Schultz, Foster Moreau, Brevin Jordan and Marlin Klein) active ahead of him. Through the Texans' first seven games, Stover had played less than half of the offensive snaps in each contest and recorded three receptions for 17 yards on five targets while rushing three times for five yards.

For the second straight week, Moreau didn't make a mark in the box score. He did technically draw a target (which he didn't catch), but it was wiped out by an accepted defensive penalty. Moreau hasn't had more than two catches in any game this season and has finished with fewer than 10 yards in every contest since Week 3, so he's not a viable fantasy play in virtually any format right now.

Ogunbowale continued to play a minor role in Houston's offense with just eight offensive snaps. He did, however, record his first touch of the campaign with a three-yard reception in the third quarter. Ogunbowale hasn't been asked to do much despite David Montgomery (groin) being sidelined since Week 5, and with Montgomery potentially getting close to a return, Ogunbowale's role on game days may soon disappear altogether.

Fairbairn was able to convert multiple field-goal attempts for the fifth straight game. The kicker made a 56-yarder in the first quarter before later adding makes from 31 and 41 yards in the fourth quarter. On the season, Fairbairn has gone 18-for-19 on field-goal tries, including 7-for-8 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far.

Marks acted as the Texans' primary running back for a fourth straight game, three of which David Montgomery has missed completely due to a groin injury. During that stretch, Marks has racked up 75 touches for 321 yards from scrimmage, but he has yet to reach the end zone since Week 4. Montgomery wasn't able to practice this week, so Marks may be in line for another role as Houston's No. 1 backfield option next Sunday at Cleveland if the former doesn't make the requisite progress in his recovery.

Not counting his 12-140-0 receiving explosion in Week 2 when Nico Collins was out with a hamstring injury, Schultz has mustered 23 grabs for 244 yards and no touchdowns across his seven other appearances. He's failed to reach 50 receiving yards in any of those contests and is merely a TE2 in fantasy.

Harrison ranked seventh on the team in targets, and although C.J. Stroud connected with four different wide receivers for five total touchdowns, Harrison was not one of them. Harrison has now reeled in six of 11 targets for 60 yards and a score over three contests with the Texans, and he will remain hard to trust from a fantasy perspective in Week 10 versus Cleveland.

In his second appearance since returning from a brutal left knee injury suffered in December 2024, Dell again recorded a reception of 40-plus yards, connecting with C.J. Stroud for a 63-yard TD in the second quarter. It was one of five touchdown passes for Stroud, who spread the ball around to nine different pass catchers and four that reached the end zone at least once. Dell will aim to build on the momentum next Sunday at Cleveland.

Boutte entered Week 9 action with a cumulative 15-194-0 line on 23 targets through seven appearances this season, so Sunday's performance was a true outburst. It didn't hurt that Boutte and his teammates were facing the only winless team in the NFL, but QB C.J. Stroud took full advantage of the opportunity, including Boutte (twice) among his five TD tosses. Ultimately, the Texans' receiving corps has a clear No. 1 in WR Nico Collins, who is the best bet among the group to produce most weeks.

Hutchinson finished tied with Kayshon Boutte for second on the team in targets behind fellow wideout Tank Dell (nine). Hutchinson was able to reach paydirt for the second straight contest, reeling in a 17-yard touchdown pass from C.J. Stroud for the team's first score of the day in the first quarter. There are many mouths to feed in Houston's passing attack, so Hutchinson will remain a volatile fantasy option ahead of the team's Week 10 matchup with the Browns.

Collins was one of four Texans to reach the end zone via a pass from QB C.J. Stroud, who tossed five TDs in all. It marked Collins' first touchdown since Week 4, when he struck twice against the Cowboys, but overall his output from week to week this season has been a bit inconsistent, as he sits on a 28-384-4 line on 39 targets through his six appearances. He'll seek better results next Sunday in Cleveland.

Stroud matched a career high with his five TD strikes, which went to Xavier Hutchinson (17 yards), Tank Dell (63), Kayshon Boutte (12 and 63) and Nico Collins (13). Moreover, Stroud's 384 passing yards matched the second most in a game in his career. He's now thrown for multiple touchdowns in four of the last five games, a stretch in which he's accounted for a remarkable 1,457 yards through the air and a 13:2 TD:INT. Stroud will attempt to keep things rolling next Sunday, when the Texans visit the Browns.
The veteran linebacker appears ready to go for Sunday's game against the winless Chargers. Al-Shaair has recorded 58 tackles (22 solo) and a pair of pass breakups across six starts this season.

Fisher hasn't played since Week 6 after undergoing thumb surgery, but he's good to go coming out of the Texans' bye week. He'll serve in a depth role at offensive tackle during Sunday's game against the Chargers.

Pitre is healthy again after missing the past two games due to an AC joint injury. The 2022 second-round pick should resume his role as the team's starting slot cornerback during Sunday's game versus the Chargers.

Jones is headed to Houston after having been released by the 49ers in late October. The 28-year-old logged two tackles across three appearances with San Francisco and will likely serve a depth role behind Tommy Togiai and Sheldon Rankins in Houston.

Noel was forced out of this past Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants after going down with the toe injury with just under nine minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. The loss of Noel is a major blow to the Texans, as he had been serving as the team's top return man in addition to emerging as a big-play threat on offense. Through Houston's first seven games, Noel had recorded 19 receptions for a team-leading 331 yards and two touchdowns and added 26 yards on four carries.

To'oTo'o ranked second on Houston in tackles behind M.J. Stewart, with whom he combined for a sack in the fourth quarter. It was just the third appearance of the campaign for To'oTo'o, who missed Weeks 2 through 5 due to a knee injury. The 25-year-old seems to be past the issue, as he's logged more than 90 percent of the Texans' defensive snaps since his return.

"We'll see. Like I said last week, he's still in that rehab process, and I'm not going to put a timetable on return," Steichen noted of the wideout, who's been on IR since Sept. 26. At 2-7, the Colts were sellers ahead of the NFL's trade deadline, so the team presumably has no reason rush Pierce back. With Keenan Allen and Josh Downs no longer in the mix, Indy's healthy WRs for now are Ashton Dulin, Laquon Treadwell, Anthony Gould, Deion Burks and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine.

Steichen also mentioned Deion Burks and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine as other candidates to fill in at the outside receiver spot opposite Laquon Treadwell, while noting that Anthony Gould will serve as the Colts' starting slot receiver after the team also traded Josh Downs to the Chiefs on Tuesday. With Alec Pierce's (heel) return from injured reserve seemingly not imminent, Dulin could have a prime opportunity to see extended snaps over the next few weeks, provided he can hold off the likes of Burks and Westbrook-Ikhine for playing time. Dulin already made a bit of a splash in the Colts' Week 9 loss to the Cowboys, connecting with Daniel Jones on a 55-yard touchdown reception while also carrying once for a three-yard gain.

With both Downs and Keenan Allen having been dealt by the Colts on Tuesday, the team will be operating with a re-shaped WR corps going forward. According to the Colts' latest unofficial depth chart, Gould is indeed listed a first-teamer along with Ashton Dulin and Laquon Treadwell. Also expected to have additional opportunities in the coming weeks will be 2026 seventh-rounder Deion Burks, with veteran pass catcher Nick Westbrook-Ikhine in the mix as well after being signed off the practice squad. Though a wait-and-see approach is in order in term's of Gould's fantasy lineup viability, his production beginning this weekend versus Miami is worth tracking by those in deeper PPR formats.

Since drawing a season-high eight targets in a Week 5 loss to the Steelers, Treadwell has barely surpassed that total over the past four games combined. Despite handling snap shares north of 70 percent in each of those contests, Treadwell has mustered a 5-58-0 receiving line on 10 targets during that stretch. The Colts will have more target volume up for grabs after trading Keenan Allen to the 49ers and Josh Downs to the Chiefs on Tuesday, and though Treadwell could be one of the beneficiaries, he still looks to be a low-upside fantasy option.

A rookie seventh-round pick out of Oklahoma, Burks has seen sparse playing time through the Colts' first nine games. He's logged less than one-third of the snaps in each of those contests and has posted a 6-60-0 receiving line on nine targets go with 21 yards on three carries. Despite his modest output to date, Burks could nonetheless be primed for more opportunities in the Indianapolis passing game over the second half of the season. Tight end Tyler Warren will likely rank as the team's top pass-catching option, but the Colts should have plenty of targets left over after trading away Keenan Allen to the 49ers and Josh Downs to the Chiefs on Tuesday. Meanwhile, top wideout Alec Pierce (heel) lacks a clear timeline to return from injured reserve.

Indianapolis will turn to Westbrook-Ikhine to fill the 53-man roster spot vacated by Keenan Allen, who was traded to the 49ers on Tuesday. Westbrook-Ikhine had previously been elevated from the Colts' practice squad for three straight games between Weeks 3 and 5 and failed to corral his lone target while logging 18 total snaps on offense. He'll fill a depth role in the Colts' receiving corps and could end up providing most of his value on the team's coverage and return units on special teams.

In order to move Taylor, Indianapolis was reportedly seeking a blockbuster trade package on par with what Carolina received in exchange for Christian McCaffrey back in 2022, but Pelissero relays that inquiring teams offered no more than a second-round pick as the best asset in any trade pitch. As a result, Taylor -- who is under contract through 2028 -- will stick around in Indianapolis through the remainder of the campaign, though it's possible that the Colts entertain trade offers for the 27-year-old running back again during the offseason.

Giddens didn't see any action after turning six carries into 43 yards in Week 8 against the Jaguars. With Jonathan Taylor potentially set to be traded before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, Giddens would stand to operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield behind rookie Seth McGowan if Taylor departs.

Shrader entered Week 9 having made just three field goals over the team's last three games, but he got back on track Sunday. The kicker made a 47-yard attempt in the third quarter before adding makes from 59 and 50 yards in the final quarter. Shrader has now converted multiple field-goal attempts in six contests this year, and he's gone 22-for-24 on field-goal tries, including 8-for-9 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

McGowan recorded his first NFL touchdown on a two-yard run in the first quarter, perhaps a harbinger of a larger role as early as next Sunday's Week 10 matchup against the Dolphins. McGowan came just a rush yard short of equaling his career-best tally in that category, and if Jonathan Taylor is indeed moved off the roster by Tuesday's trade deadline, the former would be in line to serve as the lead back moving forward.

The update settles recent trade speculation around Jones and indicates Indianapolis plans to keep him on the roster into the offseason. It's a wonder why any team was even interested in trading for Jones in the first place, as he's consistently been one of the least productive quarterbacks in the league this season. He also failed to put anything meaningful on tape Sunday in the Colts' loss to the Cowboys, completing 20 of 34 passes for 180 yards, one touchdown and one interception against one of the league's worst on-paper defenses. The touchdown was a 55-yard hookup with Ashton Dulin, where Dulin did all of the work after the catch. Jones' interception late in the fourth quarter sealed another loss for Indianapolis.

Warren tied for second in receptions and finished as the runner-up in both receiving yards and targets after a slow start to Sunday's loss. The second-year tight end's role could be even bigger by next Sunday's Week 10 home matchup against the Dolphins, as the Colts could conceivably move both Josh Downs and Jonathan Taylor, not to mention quarterback Daniel Jones, by Tuesday's trade deadline. Warren has at least four receptions in every game with the exception of Week 1 heading into the aforementioned matchup against Miami.

Alie-Cox exited in the fourth quarter and was subsequently deemed questionable to return. The veteran tight end has been a minor part of Indianapolis' offense this season, logging four catches through eight games. Alie-Cox hadn't recorded a catch or target prior to his departure Sunday.

Carlies was injured in the first half and was initially deemed questionable to return. He was then ruled out after halftime. Austin Ajiake is likely going to be asked to take on more defensive snaps in Carlies' absence.

Ogletree was able to play through his nagging knee issue in Week 8 at Jacksonville, and he'll be active again in Week 9 despite missing practice Wednesday and logging a limited practice session Thursday. He figures to continue to compete with Mo Alie-Cox and Will Mallory for snaps at tight end behind clear frontrunner Tyler Warren.

Boettcher appears to be on track to return to action Sunday versus the Cowboys after missing the team's last two contests with a groin issue. The 24-year-old will likely be back in his starting role at strongside linebacker against Dallas.

After sending out a first-round pick, two second-round picks, a fifth-round pick and a sixth-round pick Monday in separate deals to bring in defenders Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates and Davon Godchaux, the Jaguars likely could have recouped some of that draft capital if they had opted to move Thomas. Instead, Fowler indicates that the Jaguars plan to keep the rest of their roster intact ahead of the deadline, which will result in Thomas sticking around. Rather than operating as the high-volume target earner he was during his banner 2024 rookie campaign, Thomas looks like he'll continue to serve mainly as a vertical threat who frees up opportunities in the short and intermediate areas for other pass catchers. Thomas has drawn three or fewer targets in six straight games, producing a weak 4-37-2 receiving line during that stretch.

Godchaux was selected by Miami in the fifth round of the 2017 NFL Draft. Since then, he has appeared in 145 regular-season games for the Dolphins, Patriots and Saints, garnering 487 total tackles (224 solo), 5.5 sacks and three forced fumbles. Godchaux's presence will bolster depth at the defensive tackle position for the Jaguars, especially with DaVon Hamilton (knee) done for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

Oluokun tied for his team's lead in stops and notched his second sack of the season when he brought down Joe Fagnano early in the second quarter. Oluokun has been a reliable fantasy IDP asset in 2026 with at least seven tackles in six of his eight games so far. He's tallied 58 total stops, including the 2.0 sacks, along with two interceptions and a forced fumble.

Koziol was part of a three-tight-end starting unit for Jacksonville alongside Brenton Strange and Nate Boerkircher. Koziol logged the fewest offensive snaps (12) among the trio but matched both in receptions. He entered Thursday with just one catch through five contests, so it's probably not wise to count on him for substantial production moving forward.

Boerkircher was tied with Parker Washington for the second-most receiving yards on the team with 61. This game marks the fourth time this season that the rookie has surpassed 30 snaps on offense. Boerkircher has made a name for himself as Jacksonville's No. 2 option at tight end behind Brenton Strange.

Cameron didn't see the ball until the fourth quarter despite playing the third most snaps at wide receiver (25) for the Jaguars on Thursday, behind only Parker Washington (38) and Jakobi Meyers (38). This marks the third game in a row during which the 23-year-old played as the Jaguars' No. 3 option at receiver, but his limited usage keeps him as a low-priority waiver-wire add.

Abdullah recorded the third-most-offensive snaps in the backfield (seven), behind Chris Rodriguez (25) and Bayshul Tuten (20). Should everyone in the backfield remain healthy, Abdullah will likely see a similar workload for the rest of the season.

The Jaguars keep blowing teams out and aren't being pushed on offense, which is keeping Trevor Lawrence's pass volume low. Strange is still making the most of his few opportunities, totaling four grabs for 77 yards on four targets over the last two weeks, games in which the Jaguars have combined to outscore their opponents 75-17. Strange is a TE1 for fantasy and gets a date with the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

Hunter played six offensive snaps against Baltimore but turned the ball over on his only touch. After posting a 4-59-1 receiving line against the Texans in London back in Week 6, Hunter has done very little on offense. He needs the Jaguars' opponents to make games closer so the coaching staff feels obligated to utilize Hunter's big-play ability.

Rodriguez finished with just two fewer carries than Bhayshul Tuten, who came into the game managing ankle and foot injuries and was able to log a relatively abbreviated workload thanks to game script. Both backs had plenty of trouble against Baltimore's stout run defense, but Rodriguez salvaged his fantasy night with a two-yard TD run just past the midway point of the fourth quarter. Rodriguez now has scored in back-to-back games heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

The Jaguars dominated in the victory, but they fell short of the end zone enough times to keep Little busy. He didn't need to fully flex the strength of his leg, as his longest kick was from a modest 47 yards out, but Little extended his run of consecutive successful FG attempts to 10. He's now gone 14-of-16 on field-goal tries this season while converting 25 of 26 point-after attempts.

Meyers set the pace for the Jaguars in both receptions and receiving yards on the night, bouncing back nicely from a quiet 2-24-0 line just four days earlier in a blowout win over the Colts. The veteran wideout has multiple catches in all but one game, although Meyers hasn't topped 83 receiving yards in any contest to date in 2026. Meyers remains a key target for Trevor Lawrence, but he could see at least a slight boost in his outlook heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15, if Brian Thomas is moved at the trade deadline.

Lawrence unsurprisingly didn't have a high-volume night, as the Jaguars were progressively able to take control of the game with Joe Fagnano under center for the Ravens. The veteran signal-caller hit Parker Washington on a 50-yard catch-and-run touchdown over the middle just before halftime for his one scoring pass, and Lawrence connected with eight different targets overall on the night. The 2021 first overall pick has now thrown for 1,932 yards with an 18:4 TD:INT and added 79 yards on the ground heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

Washington led the Jaguars in targets while tying for second in receptions and receiving yards on the night. The fourth-year receiver snapped a two-game touchdown drought, crossing the goal line from 50 yards out on a catch and run over the middle with under a minute remaining in the first half. Washington has eclipsed 60 receiving yards in three of the past four games heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

Tuten fought through the pair of lower-body injuries that made him a game-time decision, recording his fourth rushing touchdown of the campaign on a one-yard run to cap off the opening possession of the contest. The second-year back had to grind for every yard he got on the ground, but fortunately for Tuten, the Jaguars built a comfortable enough lead where he was able to benefit from an early end to his night. Tuten has now scored in back-to-back games, and he'll have some extra time to get healthier ahead of a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

After carrying a questionable designation ahead of this contest, Walker will suit up versus the Ravens in Week 9. The 25-year-old hasn't missed a game this season, accumulating 18 total tackles (seven solo), including 3.0 sacks, in seven regular-season appearances.
inactive

Johnson was forced to miss the team's Week 8 win over the Colts while nursing an ankle injury, but he appears to be good to go for Week 9. The 25-year-old was a limited participant at the team's final practice of the week Wednesday, so he may not be back to 100 percent, but Johnson should be back in his starting role at free safety versus the Ravens.

Lane played every one of the team's defensive snaps in Week 8, stepping into a starting role in the secondary with Antonio Johnson (ankle) unavailable. The 23-year-old's biggest moment of the game came in the second quarter when he jumped in front of a pass from Colts quarterback Daniel Jones for an interception, returning it 92 yards for his first career defensive touchdown. Lane has now compiled 20 total tackles (10 solo) and four passes defensed, including Sunday's pick-six, over seven contests during the 2026 campaign.

injuries.evidence: It was already known Murray suffered a season-ending elbow injury during the first quarter of Sunday's game versus the Colts, so the move comes as no big surprise.
injuries.detail: It was already known Murray suffered a season-ending elbow injury during the first quarter of Sunday's game versus the Colts, so the move comes as no big surprise. In his absence, 2025 sixth-rounder Rayuan Lane could step into a starting role at safety for the rest of the year.

The Chiefs' backup quarterback saw the field for just the second time this season, after he had previously played one snap in a Week 1 win over the Broncos. Due to head coach Andy Reid's reluctance to use starter Patrick Mahomes on quarterback sneaks, Fields subbed into the game for a third-and-1 play in the first quarter. Fields ended up coughing the football, with the Jets making the recovery. The Chiefs went on to build enough of a lead to rest Mahomes for the final possession of the game with just over two minutes left in the fourth quarter, when Fields proceeded to hand the ball off three times before kneeling to run out the clock.

Royals ranked fourth among KC wideouts in offensive snaps (21), trailing Xavier Worthy (49), Rashee Rice (38) and Andrew Armstrong (22). Royals matched his season high with two catches, and the 18 receiving yards were his second-most in a game this season. That speaks to the minimal production he's provided thus far, and Royals' role could be further reduced with the Chiefs' acquisition of Josh Downs on Tuesday.

questionable

Gray was a minor factor in the passing game, with his lone reception gaining 11 yards late in the third quarter. Meanwhile, No. 1 tight end Travis Kelce paced Kansas City with 72 receiving yards on four catches. Gray had a nice two-game run with a combined six catches for 97 yards across Weeks 6 and 7, but since then he's tallied just three receptions for 26 yards and a touchdown across his subsequent two games.

Allen made the start at wide receiver but ran just 13 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 36 dropbacks against New York. With Xavier Worthy (hamstring) now injured, Allen could have a path to more playing time moving forward, but all three of Rashee Rice, Kenneth Walker and Travis Kelce are well ahead of the rookie wideout for targets.

Moore suffered an ankle injury in Sunday's win over the Jets. While he hasn't been ruled out for Week 10 versus the Falcons, there's certainly the possibility of an absence. If that's the case, Joshua Ezeudu may fill the void at right tackle.

The same applies to QB Patrick Mahomes (elbow), with the status of both key Kansas City skill players worth monitoring closely in the coming days. If Worthy is limited or out this weekend, added reps behind top WR Rashee Rice will be available for some combination of Cyrus Allen, Jalen Royals and Andrew Armstrong.

Mahomes emerged from Week 9 action with what Ian Rapoport of NFL Network described earlier Monday as an elbow "strain/sprain" to his throwing arm following an MRI on Sunday. For his part, Reid also noted with regard to the star QB's exam results that "it was more positive news than negative news. It looks like it's just a matter of rehabbing and getting rid of some of the soreness." As a result, look for Mahomes' practice participation to be managed this week, which could lead to his top backup Justin Fields logging some added reps in the coming days.

The Chiefs held a 28-12 lead by the end of three quarters, which provided the opportunity for head coach Andy Reid to give Kenneth Walker, who scored three total touchdowns, some down time in the latter portion of the contest. Johnson took advantage of his opportunities, recording a six-yard touchdown run with 3:35 remaining. The rookie fifth-round pick's yardage total was a new career high, while his carry tally was his highest since Week 3. Johnson will remain in a modest No. 2 role for a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons next Sunday.

Rice led the Chiefs in targets while finishing as the runner-up in both receptions and receiving yards. The veteran receiver has been busy the last two games while turning 15 targets into a 12-102-1 line, but he has just one catch of 20-plus yards in that span. Rice is averaging a relatively modest 11.7 yards per catch heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons.

Kelce led the Chiefs in receiving yards and finished second in targets on the afternoon, and his tally in the former category also served as the legendary tight end's second highest of the season. Kelce got there with a big boost from a game-high 38-yard catch, and he'll take a formidable 33-482-2 line into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons next Sunday.

Butker pushed his only field-goal try wide right from 51 yards out in the final moments of the first half. The kicker has now gone 12-for-19 on field-goal attempts this season, and head coach Andy Reid was asked about Butker's future following the game, stating that he'll "address that" as the team prepares for Week 10, per Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star. The team signed veteran Justin Tucker to the practice squad in late October, and Tucker could get a shot with the active roster in Butker's place.

Walker put together another one of his signature high-efficiency performances on the ground, averaging 5.7 yards per carry in the process. He contributed a seven-yard touchdown reception on the first play of the second quarter, and he struck again as a receiver via a 25-yard scoring grab with just over five minutes remaining in the first half. Walker capped off the highly fantasy-friendly day with his seventh rushing touchdown of the season, a two-yard run in the waning moments of the third quarter. Walker is up to 872 rushing yards, 172 receiving yards and 11 total touchdowns heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons next Sunday.

The 27-year-old was questionable due to a hip issue, but it's no surprise he's suiting up after putting in full practice sessions Thursday and Friday. Remigio has played just two offensive snaps this year but has operated as Kansas City's primary return man and should continue to do so Sunday.

injuries.evidence: Sneed will be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 12 against the Bills on Thursday, Nov.
injuries.detail: Sneed was initially given the questionable tag for Sunday's game against the Broncos. He's been able to play through a lingering knee issue, but his placement on IR indicates that the injury has gotten to the point that an extended absence is warranted for the seventh-year defensive back. Sneed will be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 12 against the Bills on Thursday, Nov. 26. Jaden Hicks, Jadon Canady, Kristian Fulton and Christian Roland-Wallace are all candidates to see more work in the secondary due to the absences of both Sneed and Mansoor Delane (shoulder) for Sunday's AFC West tilt.

injuries.evidence: The Chiefs now have 21 days to activate Norman-Lott from the PUP list, otherwise he would be forced to miss the entire 2026 season.
injuries.detail: Norman-Lott was limited in his return to practice Wednesday. He's in the final stages of his recovery from a torn ACL that he sustained in October of 2025. The Chiefs now have 21 days to activate Norman-Lott from the PUP list, otherwise he would be forced to miss the entire 2026 season.

Conner was on the field for every single defensive snap for a second consecutive game following the Chiefs' Week 5 bye. He missed the first three games of the regular season due to a knee injury but has suited up for each of the team's last three contests, during which he has accumulated 17 tackles (nine solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defense.

The second-year defensive back's 10 tackles were a career best, and his interception off Sam Darnold late in the second quarter was also the first of Williams' NFL career. Williams is up to 29 tackles (17 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and seven pass defenses (including one interception) through six regular-season games.

Bolton played all but one of the Chiefs' 69 defensive snaps during Sunday's loss, and he finished second on the team in tackles behind Drue Tranquill (12). Bolton has recorded double-digit stops in four of six regular-season games and is up to 59 tackles (29 solo) and two pass defenses on the year.

Bech logged a 34 percent offensive snap share, third-highest among Raiders wideouts behind Jalen Nailor (74 percent) and Tre Tucker (64 percent). Though he seems fairly secure in the No. 3 wideout role, Bech hasn't done much this season, producing no more than three catches or 25 yards in any of his five games to date.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft has opened his professional career on the bench, with his lone action to date coming during garbage time of a blowout loss to the Patriots in Week 5. However, with the 4-5 Raiders shipping out Cousins for a 2027 third-round pick, the 23-year-old Mendoza will now be thrust into his first extended NFL playing time and will face a pair of tough defenses off the bat, as he'll follow up the matchup against the Seahawks with a road game in Denver in Week 11. Mendoza had underwhelming numbers over his three preseason appearances (25-for-45 passing for 240 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions with four carries for 15 yards), but he's reportedly been "tearing it up in practice" during the regular season and has given the Raiders optimism that he's ready to lead the offense, per Matt Zenitz of CBSSports.com.
questionable

Gay's lone field goal came from 50 yards in the second quarter, and he now has made three of his four kicks from 50 yards or longer on the season. The 32-year-old is 19-for-21 on field-goal attempts and a perfect 21-for-21 on extra-point tries across nine appearances.

Nailor was a non-factor on offense in Week 9, failing to reach double-digit receiving yards for the fourth time this season. The wide receiver has had a hard time getting into a groove in his first season with Las Vegas, catching 14 of 28 targets for 122 yards and a touchdown over eight contests so far.

The tight end was inches and a couple breaks away from having a much bigger afternoon, as he lost a fumble just before crossing the goal line on what would have been a 25-yard touchdown. He then had another score called back on a penalty in the second half. Mayer has alternated big games with down ones this season, and he'll try to rebound next Sunday in a tough spot against the Seahawks' strong defense.

The rookie running back wasn't targeted in the passing game. One week after getting a trial run as the Raiders' clear lead back, a game in which he produced 83 yards on 25 carries, Washington was out-snapped 32 to 17 by Ashton Jeanty against San Francisco. He's averaging just 3.9 yards per carry on 71 totes this season and has just three receptions, though it's worth noting that Jeanty has been even less efficient as a ball carrier with only 3.1 YPC. Washington is a fantasy bench stash, but the Raiders' rushing attack seems broken as a whole.

Tucker finished tied for the team lead in targets with tight end Brock Bowers, garnering at least five targets for the fifth time in the team's last six contests. The wide receiver rebounded well after being blanked in Week 8 versus the Jets, securing four or more receptions for the seventh time this season. Tucker has now reeled in 33 of 56 targets for 529 yards and four touchdowns over the Raiders' first nine games during the 2026 campaign.

The Raiders largely abandoned the run after going down 14-0 early, but Jeanty was more effective with his six carries than Mike Washington, who rushed six times for minus-3 yards and finished without a target. Sunday's even distribution in carries was a positive development for Jeanty, who had just two rushing attempts to Washington's 25 in the Week 8 win over the Jets. Jeanty still has more receiving yards (371) than rushing yards (362) and is averaging just 3.2 yards per carry heading into a difficult Week 10 matchup against Seattle's elite front seven.

Bowers had a 21-yard touchdown reception in the third quarter and came one yard short of scoring again on a 33-yard catch on a fourth-quarter drive that ended with a Kirk Cousins interception in the end zone. The star TE has reached 70 receiving yards in all seven of his appearances this season and is up to six touchdowns. Bowers came five receiving yards shy of his season high and continues to roll, even as the 4-5 Raiders drop out of contention in the AFC. He'll likely face more resistance in Week 10 against the Seahawks, who just held Cardinals TE Trey McBride to 54 yards.

Zuhn is done for the day after sustaining a concussion in the third quarter. Caleb Rogers has taken over at right guard in his absence, and Zuhn will now have to clear the league's concussion protocol before he can return to the field.

Porter suffered a groin injury last Sunday against the Jets and logged a DNP/LP/FP practice progression this week. He was questionable to suit up entering Sunday but will ultimately be able to give it a go. Porter ranks second on the Raiders with five defensed passes on the season.

Dean was able to notch exactly 12 stops for the fourth game in a row and fifth time this season. The linebacker is out to a great start to his first campaign in Las Vegas, registering 80 total tackles (38 solo), including 1.5 sacks, while also adding an interception and three forced fumbles over eight contests so far.

Chinn had quite a day in Week 8, finishing second on the team in takedowns while also jumping in front of a deep ball from Jets quarterback Geno Smith for the safety's first interception of the year. Chinn has now compiled 56 total tackles (38 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding two forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries and an interception over eight contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

White was released by the team Tuesday to make room for Carter Runyon (foot), who was activated off injured reserve. With Runyon now waived and potentially joining the Raiders' practice squad, White was re-signed. To date, the 27-year-old has had the best season of his career, amassing eight catches (19 targets) for 112 yards and three touchdowns.

Lambert-Smith wasn't exactly prolific in spite of logging a hearty 40 offensive snaps, but he made his one catch count, hauling in a 50-yard reception in the third quarter. However, the woeful Chargers turned the ball over on a fumble two plays later. Lambert-Smith has spent much of the season on IR and has had an inconsistent role when suiting up, but he was deployed pretty heavily Sunday because Ladd McConkey couldn't play due to back spasms. If McConkey is also sidelined next Monday in Baltimore, Lambert-Smith could again be a fairly big part of Los Angeles' air attack.

The Chargers continue to use a three-man backfield, an unfriendly fantasy situation and one to avoid when making lineup decisions each week. Vidal has been productive when he does get touches, rushing 36 times for 162 yards (4.5 YPC) and one touchdown across eight games. He's also caught 10 passes for 56 yards and an additional score.

Gadsden was on the field for 33 of 72 offensive snaps (45.8 percent), which was second-most among Chargers tight ends behind Charlie Kolar (47). Gadsden has caught two passes or fewer in six of eight regular-season games, and his 19-172-1 receiving line (on 29 targets) is well behind pace from his rookie campaign (49 catches on 69 targets for 664 yards and three scores across 15 regular-season contests). The Chargers' offense this season has struggled under quarterback Justin Herbert and coordinator Mike McDaniel, which doesn't bring much confidence ahead of their Week 10 road tilt against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.

Kolar has recorded three catches in four of his last five outings, although he's cracked 30-plus receiving yards in just two of those contests. The Chargers average a season-low 15.1 points per game, and their 201.9 receiving yards per game is ninth-fewest in the NFL, making pass catchers like Kolar hard to rely on for sustained production. The 0-8 Chargers will look to capture their first win of the season in Week 10 against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.

Herbert may still have to manage some discomfort in the finger during Monday's contest, but since the injury to his non-throwing hand, he shouldn't be too affected while throwing or handing the ball off. That being said, Herbert has become increasingly difficult to justify including in fantasy lineups even when he's been in more optimal health entering games. Heading into the matchup with the Ravens, Herbert has completed a career-low 61.3 percent of his passes for 6.8 yards per attempt and just six touchdowns in eight games. He's tied with New England's Drake Maye for the league lead in interceptions thrown (11) and ranks second behind Cleveland's Deshaun Watson in sacks taken (31).

Harris failed to take advantage of Ladd McConkey (back) failing to appear in Sunday's game, registering his fewest receiving yards in a game this season. Harris was able to garner a team-high seven targets, which bodes well for his chances of increased production in Week 10 against the Ravens if McConkey remains sidelined.

McConkey was not among the Chargers' Week 9 inactives, but he didn't play any snaps in Sunday's loss to the Texans after experiencing back spasms during pregame workouts. Harbaugh's assessment that the wideout is 'day-to-day' offers hope that McConkey will be in the clear ahead of next Monday's game against the Ravens, and a big step toward that outcome would be his full participation in practice no later than Saturday.

Dicker was able to make multiple field-goal tries for the third straight game and fifth time this season. The kicker did all his damage in the first half, converting field goals from 52, 33 and 43 yards before the break. Dicker has now gone 15-for-17 on field-goal attempts, including 1-for-2 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

Uiagalelei was inaccurate in his first taste of regular-season NFL action but threw a 15-yard touchdown pass to Derius Davis. If Herbert isn't available to face the Ravens on MNF in Week 10 and Trey Lance (groin) isn't ready to return from injured reserve, Uiagalelei would presumably be tabbed for the first regular-season start of the latter's career.

Johnston's long touchdown catch cut the deficit to 38-15 in the fourth quarter. That was the final pass Justin Herbert (finger) completed before exiting the game. If Herbert can't play against the Ravens in Week 10, Johnston would likely find himself catching passes from DJ Uiagalelei. Johnston's 58 receiving yards set a new season high, surpassing his one-catch, 57-yard effort in Week 6, and Sunday's TD was his first of the season.

Mitchell led LA's three-man backfield rotation with 67 scrimmage yards, while Omarion Hampton had 60 and Kimani Vidal contributed 36. Mitchell's fumble came late in the third quarter, with the Chargers already trailing 31-9 at the time. The winless Chargers are averaging a league-low 15.1 points per game heading into a Week 10 trip to Baltimore, and things could get even worse if QB Justin Herbert (finger) has to miss time after getting injured in the fourth quarter.

Hampton worked as the Chargers' primary rushing option ahead of Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal, who recorded seven carries apiece. The 0-8 Chargers unsurprisingly faced another negative game script, though, and Hampton wasn't involved in the passing game. The 2025 first-round pick continues to disappoint on a surprisingly awful offense that could get even worse should QB Justin Herbert (finger) miss any additional action after exiting in the fourth quarter. Hampton will try to snap a four-game touchdown drought in Week 10 against the Ravens.

With Justin Herbert (finger) out of the game and the score out of hand already, Davis caught a 15-yard touchdown from backup DJ Uiagalelei in the fourth quarter. Davis has no fantasy value as a reserve wideout in one of the league's worst offenses.
Hart exited the third quarter of Sunday's game with an ankle injury. Rodney Shelley will play outside cornerback opposite Donte Jackson while Hart undergoes further evaluation.
The special-teamer will not return to Sunday's contest after exiting in the first quarter. A number of players could step up to contribute on special teams in Waxter's absence.
Eboigbe was hurt in the first quarter, and his return is uncertain. Nick Barrett will likely pick up more defensive snaps for as long as Eboigbe remains sidelined.

Perryman logged a pair of limited sessions during Week 9 prep but is not quite ready to return to the Chargers' 53-man roster. The inside linebacker will continue his recovery during Week 10 prep in the hopes of making his 2026 regular-season debut soon.

Njoku returned to practice this week but was limited all three days before being deemed doubtful for Week 9 action. The TE's next chance to play will arrive Monday, Nov. 16, when the Chargers face the Ravens.

Shelley missed each of Los Angeles' past three games while tending to an ankle injury. However, he followed two limited practices to begin this week with a full session Friday to position himself for a return Sunday. Shelley has played a rotational role in the secondary when active this season while also contributing on special teams.

Jackson missed each of the Chargers' past three games due to a hamstring injury, but he was able to log a full practice session Friday and is set to return to action versus Houston. Before getting hurt, he started in three of his four appearances to begin the season, so he'll likely return to that role Sunday, especially since fellow cornerback Deane Leonard (concussion) has been ruled out.
doubtful

Higbee was held to just one catch for a second consecutive game, although his 13-yard grab set the Rams up on the Commanders' one yard line and led to a rushing touchdown by Blake Corum on the next play. Higbee has only four catches over his last three games, but he figures to play a larger role in the passing game for at least the next month while Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is on injured reserve. The Rams will hit the road for Week 10 against the Cardinals, whose defense has given up six touchdowns to opposing tight ends this season, which ranks 25th in the NFL.

Atwell ended up finishing second among Rams wide receivers in both targets and offensive snaps behind Puka Nacua. However, the Rams' offense will have to undergo a sizable overhaul in the absence of Nacua, who suffered a sprained PCL/MCL in his knee as well as turf toe during Sunday's win, with the superstar wide receiver expected to be sidelined for at least a month while on injured reserve, per Sarah Bishop of ESPN.com. Davante Adams (hamstring) is also on injured reserve, so that leaves Atwell and Konata Mumpfield as the top healthy wide receivers on the Rams' 53-man roster, and rookie sixth-rounder CJ Daniels is also in position for a larger role on offense. The Rams will face the Cardinals in Week 10, and Arizona's defense has given up 19 passing touchdowns on the year, which is second-most in the league behind Las Vegas' 20.

Despite the lack of production, Mumpfield's 20 receiving yards ended up being second-most on the Rams behind Puka Nacua (150). The bigger news from Sunday's game was Nacua sustaining a PCL/MCL sprain in his knee and turf toe, and the superstar wide receiver is expected to miss at least one month while on injured reserve, per Sarah Bishop of ESPN.com. With Davante Adams (hamstring) also on IR until at least Week 11, that leaves the Rams with Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and rookie sixth-rounder CJ Daniels as the top wide receivers for Matthew Stafford. The Rams hit the road for Week 10 against the Cardinals, whose defense has given up 19 passing touchdowns, which is second-most in the NFL behind the Raiders (20).

This is another blow to the Rams' receiving corps, as Davante Adams (hamstring) is still on IR and Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is slated to miss several weeks. Whittington would have had a chance to carve out a major role in Los Angeles' wideout room, but instead he'll be sidelined until at least Dec. 20. The Rams signed Xavier Smith off San Francisco's practice squad Tuesday to take Whittington's place on the 53-man roster and in the WR corps.

Smith had been with the Rams early in the campaign before being waived Oct. 2. He subsequently signed with San Francisco's practice squad, where he had resided until Los Angeles brought him back into the fold Tuesday. Smith drew just one target (which he didn't catch) across 80 offensive snaps over his three games with the Rams in the early portion of the season, but he could immediately factor into the mix for the next several weeks, as Davante Adams (hamstring) is still on IR, Puka Nacua (knee) is slated to miss several weeks and Jordan Whittington (back) landed on injured reserve Tuesday. Smith could also be used as a returner in Whittington's absence.

After missing five consecutive games while recovering from an ankle sprain, Ferguson appeared poised to return from IR ahead of this past Sunday's game against the Commanders, but his activation was delayed after he pulled his hamstring while running a route during Friday's practice. McVay said after the practice that the setback would likely keep Ferguson out for "a couple more weeks." Ferguson's 21-day window will come to a close Nov. 25, so even if he doesn't resume practicing before then, he'll likely need to show the Rams that he's made at least some progress in his recovery from the hamstring injury to get activated. McVay said that he would be open to adding Ferguson back to the 53-man roster before he's ready to play, but the Rams may not be keen on essentially playing a man down for more than a game or two.

Parkinson ranked second on Los Angeles in receptions, though he didn't turn them into many yards. Still, it was his third straight contest with at least four catches, so Parkinson looks to be developing into a favorite target of QB Matthew Stafford. That could come in handy in Week 10 and beyond, as Stafford is going to need to turn to other pass catchers to help make up for the massive production being lost in the absence of Puka Nacua, who is expected to land on IR due to knee and turf-toe injuries.

McManus' field goals were good from 33 and 20 yards, and he's now made all 13 of his kicks through three games with Los Angeles. With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) now out for the foreseeable future, this offense figures to struggle to score points, downgrading McManus in the fantasy kicker rankings.

McVay said part of the decision whether to place Avila on IR will be influenced by concerns that the team could use up all of its eight injured-reserve slots for players eligible to return later in the season. Either way, for as long as Avila remains sidelined, 2024 sixth rounder Beaux Limmer projects to fill in at left guard.

Making his return from a knee injury that had sidelined him since Week 1, Garrett made an immediate impact and accounted for three of the Rams' four sacks of Jayden Daniels on the afternoon, with Braden Fiske and Shaun Dolac splitting the other. A healthy Garrett's presence in the front seven changes the entire complexion of the defense, and he could continue to make up for lost time in Week 10 against Gardner Minshew and the Cardinals.

The Rams' backfield has become a full-fledged timeshare, with Corum getting double-digit carries for a third straight game and out-producing Kyren Williams on the ground in Washington. Corum has gotten into the end zone in all three of those contests, punching in a one-yard score in the third quarter Sunday, and over that stretch he's amassed 224 rushing yards and three TDs while averaging 5.7 yards a carry. With Puka Nacua (knee) headed for an MRI, the Rams could lean even more heavily on their ground attack in a Week 10 tilt against the Cardinals.

The veteran QB looked the way of Puka Nacua (knee) early and often, with no other Ram pass catcher managing more than 20 receiving yards, and the star wideout was on the other end of a seven-yard TD toss in the fourth quarter that proved to be the winning score. Stafford has thrown a single touchdown pass in back-to-back games after producing multiple TDs in five of six contests before that, and his options could get even thinner with Nacua headed for an MRI after getting hurt on L.A.'s final possession.

Blake Corum was the more productive Ram on the ground, turning 11 carries into 58 yards and a touchdown, but the offense mainly flowed through Puka Nacua on the afternoon. Williams failed to find the end zone for only the third time in nine games this season, and the 45 rushing yards were his lowest total since Week 1, although he has yet to reach 100 in any contest. The Los Angeles backfield has become a clear timeshare however, limiting Williams' upside heading into a Week 10 trip to Arizona.

Stuard finished the week as a limited participant in Friday's practice due to a hamstring injury that occurred during Week 8 warmups. The 28-year-old has played in all eight Rams games this season, recording two total tackles (one solo).

Curl is set to suit up for Sunday's game despite missing the Rams' Wednesday and Thursday practice sessions. The strong safety will need to anchor the team's secondary due to the absence of starting cornerbacks Jaylen Watson (shoulder, IR) and Trent McDuffie (back).

Watson exited Sunday's win over the Chargers early with a severe shoulder injury. The cornerback will undergo surgery while on IR, which will end his season. Watson ends the season with 24 tackles (14 solo) and nine passes defensed, including one interception, over seven regular-season games.

Rivers missed six games while on injured reserve with a calf injury he sustained in the Rams' Week 2 loss to the Giants. The 27-year-old has returned ahead of Sunday's game against the Commanders and has no injury designation headed into the contest. Rivers will likely be a special-teams contributor with no real role in the Rams' offense.

Coleman logged just 11 offensive snaps, and he's settled back in as the Dolphins' fourth receiver with all three of Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell healthy ahead of him on the depth chart. Coleman, a fifth-round rookie out of Missouri has no fantasy appeal.

The Dolphins completed just 14 passes against Detroit, and Bell had his fourth zero-catch game of the season. With Caleb Douglas and Malik Washington healthy, Bell is the WR3 in an offense that can barely even support one pass catcher in the box score most weeks. Bell has 12 grabs for 148 yards and no touchdowns on 27 targets through eight games.

This move was anticipated after Sieler suffered a ruptured biceps in Sunday's Week 9 loss to the Lions. The veteran defensive tackle is scheduled for surgery and will finish his ninth NFL campaign with 24 tackles, including 2.0 sacks. Zeek Biggers, Kenneth Grant and Jordan Phillips could all take on more defensive snaps with Sieler sidelined for the rest of the season.

A 2025 sixth-round pick of the Eagles, McCord will be making his NFL debut Sunday, after he had been active for each of the 1-7 Dolphins' first eight games but didn't see any playing time behind Willis. Before landing with the Dolphins in a trade prior to Week 1, the 24-year-old signal-caller looked sharp during preseason action as a member of the Packers, completing 46 of 70 passes for 446 yards and a 4:0 TD:INT while adding 16 yards on five carries over three games. Expectations should still be held in check for McCord in his first regular-season action, especially while he'll be working with one of the NFL's weaker collections of skill-position players. The Dolphins are optimistic that Willis will be able to return from IR before the end of the season, but McCord should be primed for at least a four-game run as the team's starter while Willis is sidelined.

Miami now has used the maximum three standard elevations on Gonzalez, and he's made just five of seven field-goal attempts and all five PATs across three games. The Dolphins will need to sign the kicker to the active roster if he's going to keep kicking for the team moving forward.

Allen's catch came on a fake punt, so it was an outlier of a play. He played just six offensive snaps behind clear RB1 Ollie Gordon. Since joining Miami via waivers last month, Allen has logged 31 snaps on special teams and six on offense. He has no fantasy appeal.

Entering play Sunday, Dulcich produced 13 grabs for 166 yards over his previous three games, but he took a big step back against Detroit on a day Malik Willis didn't have any answers, as he passed for just 128 yards. Dulcich doesn't catch touchdowns and plays in a low-volume, low-scoring offense, making him more of a TE2 headed into Week 10 against the Colts.

Washington was held in check by Detroit's suspect secondary, failing to reel in at least three passes for the first time this season. In addition, his 21 receiving yards were also a season low. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 70 receiving yards in a game this year, and he has reached the end zone only once. Washington will have an opportunity to get back on track against the sputtering Colts in Week 10.

Douglas led the Dolphins in receptions, receiving yards and targets, as the rookie third-round pick continued to profile as one of Malik Willis' most reliable targets. Douglas' catch and target totals were also new career highs, while his yardage tally tied for the second highest of his nascent NFL tenure. Douglas should continue to play a key role in Miami's air attack over the second half of the season as the Dolphins look to continue cultivating their young talent.

Gordon worked in the lead role as expected but found running room at a premium against a game Lions defense. Gordon has at least Sunday's carry total in four straight games, but he's now seen his rushing yardage total decline in consecutive games. Jaylen Wright's inactive status due to a quadriceps injury helped Gordon's touch floor overall, and the latter should remain the top option in Miami's ground attack in a favorable Week 10 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

Kacmarek took a low hit after making a catch in the third quarter and subsequently went to the medical tent. He then returned to the sideline and tested out the injured leg, so he appears to be at least attempting to re-enter the contest. If Kacmarek can't return, however, Greg Dulcich and Seydou Traore will be Miami's two healthy active tight ends.

Herring suffered a neck injury in the Week 8 loss to New England. Despite logging three limited practices throughout the week and being listed as questionable, he's good to go for the meeting with Detroit. The 28-year-old has appeared in seven regular-season games in 2026, accruing nine total tackles (four solo) and 1.0 sacks.

Proctor suffered a concussion in Week 7 against the Jets and didn't play this past Sunday versus New England. However, he was a full participant in all three of Miami's practices this week and has cleared concussion protocol. Proctor is therefore set to reclaim his starting role at left guard.

Rodriguez fell three tackles shy of Jordyn Brooks' team-leading total as the Dolphins dropped to 1-6. The rookie second-round pick's 12 tackles over the past two games mark the most fallow two-game stretch of Rodriguez's young career in that category. He'll try to pick up the pace in Week 9 against the Lions.

Jefferson had averaged a career-low 56.1 receiving yards per game through the first eight contests while the Vikings had the likes of Kyler Murray (hamstring), Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer under center, but the star receiver looks to be one of the biggest winners in the aftermath of the deadline. He'll be reunited with Cousins, who was at the helm for Jefferson's first four years in the league, when the wideout averaged 98.0 yards per contest and had a 17-game pace of 1,671 and 8.5 touchdowns. Though Cousins is three years older from when he last donned a Vikings uniform, he enjoyed a resurgent start to the season in Las Vegas, ranking second in the NFL in passing touchdowns (20) and fifth in passing yards (2,340) despite playing behind a weak offensive line and working with an underwhelming receiver group. Cousins' hot start and history with Jefferson should give Jefferson's fantasy managers added confidence in his rest-of-season outlook.

Felton continues to handle a muted role as a depth receiver for Minnesota, as Monday marked the third consecutive game in which he played single-digit snaps. For the season, the second-year wideout out of Maryland has been limited to just three receptions for 41 yards on seven targets over eight appearances.

Dallas notched just eight offensive snaps but also contributed 19 snaps on special teams. The veteran running back went without a carry for the fourth time over Minnesota's past five games, indicating his lack of a role in the running game. Overall this season, Dallas has been a very small part of the Vikings' offense, recording four carries for 14 yards and five catches for 36 yards (on five targets) through eight contests.

Price wasn't the only Minnesota pass catcher who logged an inefficient line, as starting quarterback Carson Wentz completed just eight of 25 pass attempts. Price did make an impact in the return game by averaging 31.0 yards on his four kickoff returns. Price's role continues to be mostly centered on special teams, as he's caught just four passes for 32 yards on 11 targets through eight games.

After missing his lone field-goal attempt in Week 8 against the Lions, Reichard bounced back Monday to connect on field goals from 43 and 53 yards in the second quarter, which ended up being the only points that the Vikings scored. Reichard's 20 made field goals through eight regular-season games is tied for fourth-most in the NFL, and his seven makes from 50-plus yards is tied with Ka'imi Fairbairn for second behind Spencer Shrader (eight). The Vikings are 6-2 despite their struggles on offense this season, but the acquisition of Kirk Cousins from the Raiders on Tuesday should elevate Richard's week-to-week scoring potential. Minnesota will travel to Lambeau Field for Week 10 against Green Bay on Nov. 15.

He will likely play a similar backup role behind newly acquired Kirk Cousins as the season progresses, at least until Kyler Murray returns from a hamstring injury.

Signed off the practice squad ahead of Monday's game against the Bills, Beckham made his Vikings debut in the 23-6 loss, going without a target while playing just two snaps on offense. He'll end up giving up his spot on the 53-man roster just one day later after the Vikings brought in quarterback Kirk Cousins in a trade with the Raiders prior to the deadline, but Beckham won't be without a home for long. Per Tom Pelissero of Netflix, Beckham is expected to re-sign with the Vikings' practice squad and will be eligible to be elevated for three games.

Addison finished third in receptions and receiving yards on the night for a low-volume Vikings passing game, and his final catch, which went for 16 yards, came on Minnesota's last drive from the arm of Max Brosmer. Carson Wentz's game-long ineffectiveness depressed the production of the air attack as a whole, but Addison would be in better position to boost his numbers if Kyler Murray (hamstring) is able to return for Sunday's Week 10 road matchup against the Packers.

Jones and backfield mate Jordan Mason combined for just 11 carries on an abysmal night for the Vikings offense, and the latter was much more efficient than Jones by averaging 5.8 yards per carry on his six totes. Jones now has seen his rushing yardage totals drop in three straight games, and Mason's return from injured reserve has played a role in the former seeing just 18 total carries in the last three contests. Jones retains a very modest outlook for a Week 10 road matchup against his old Packers teammates Sunday.

Mason was markedly more efficient than backfield mate Aaron Jones with his opportunities, averaging 5.8 yards per carry compared to the latter's 3.2. Both backs' touches were limited due to game script, however, but Mason's YPC was an encouraging figure. The veteran back next takes aim at the Packers defense in a Week 10 road matchup on Sunday.

In addition to leading the Vikings in receptions, Hockenson finished second in receiving yardage and targets in a rough performance by Minnesota's offense. The veteran wideout has hauled in exactly four catches in four straight games, though he snapped a two-game TD streak Monday. It remains to be seen who will be throwing passes for Minnesota next Sunday in Green Bay, as Carson Wentz struggled enormously Monday and Kyler Murray currently is dealing with a Grade 2 hamstring strain.

Wentz had typically put together competent performances in his opportunities to lead head coach Kevin O'Connell's offense in the past, but Monday night was a clear exception. Wentz took only one sack, but he banged up his right hand on a first-half pass attempt, then had his foot stepped on by offensive lineman Joe Huber in the second half, the latter of which required a visit to the medical tent. Wentz also repeatedly failed to master what had been a vulnerable Bills pass defense, averaging a minuscule 3.2 yards per attempt. He tossed interceptions on back-to-back drives to open the second half as well, and although they only led to one field goal for Buffalo, they were indicative of the kind of night it was for the veteran signal-caller. Wentz ultimately was pulled for Max Brosmer for the Vikings' final drive, and if Murray can't suit up for a Week 10 road showdown with the Packers on Sunday, it remains to be seen if Wentz will get another crack at a starting assignment.
Levi Drake Rodriguez, Elijah Williams and Jalen Redmond will handle more of the defensive-line duties with Ingram-Dawkins sidelined.

Van Noy was briefly sidelined with a calf injury in the first quarter, but he has now returned to action. The 35-year-old will continue to operate in his primary reserve role at weak-side linebacker versus the Bills.

Van Ginkel was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday but was able to upgrade to full participation Saturday. He's thus clear to suit up on Monday Night Football against the Bills. That's a big deal for the Vikings in their quest to slow down Josh Allen, as Van Ginkel leads the team with 6.5 sacks through seven games.
Darrisaw began Week 9 prep with a limited session Thursday, but he was able to log a full session Friday. As such, he should be good to go for Monday's matchup against Buffalo.

Both of Larison's tackles came while on kickoff coverage, and his lone touch on offense took place early in the fourth quarter. TreVeyon Henderson (illness) doesn't have a clear timeline of return, so Larison and Corey Kiner are currently slated to be the Patriots' top backfield options for Week 10 against the Lions in Detroit.

With Mack Hollins (calf) back in the lineup, Williams still held a big snap share, playing 78 percent of the Patriots' offensive snaps against Green Bay. Efton Chism (51 percent) was the biggest loser in terms of playing time. Williams has earned just 15 targets across nine games this season, catching seven passes for 190 yards and two touchdowns.

Even with Hunter Henry (foot) active, Raridon out-targeted the veteran six to three and produced 52 yards to Henry's 35 on the same amount of catches. Raridon has been a big-play threat as a rookie, averaging 14.1 yards per catch on 16 grabs this season, turning his 26 targets into 225 yards and two touchdowns. He's one of the better back-end TE2 options in fantasy.
